# Mod Hermes: what clanker changes, adds, or configures in Hermes

## Purpose

[V1_SCOPE.md](V1_SCOPE.md) defines what clanker v1 must do. This document defines **what has to change in or around Hermes** to get there, one section per capability. Each section is a small PRD: the stock behavior, the requirements, the approach, and the acceptance checks.

Pinned upstream: Hermes `v2026.9.24`, commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f` ([baseline](verification/hermes/baseline.json)). Source paths are relative to `.local/hermes-lab/upstream/`. Findings cite the audits in [verification/](verification/); re-check line numbers before patching.

## Conventions

Every requirement is tagged with how it is delivered, in order of preference:

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Config** | Stock Hermes setting. No code. |
| **Ext** | Supported extension point: plugin hook, vault backend, toolset selection, relay contract. |
| **Patch** | Change to Hermes source. Kept as a small, named patch set against the pinned commit. |
| **Clanker** | New code outside Hermes (connector, trusted handler, vault web app, pool manager). TypeScript preferred. |

Status words: **Verified** (read in pinned source or reproduced by a probe), **Assumed** (believed, not yet checked), **Open** (needs a decision or investigation).

Every Patch must be listed in the [patch register](#patch-register) with its reason and whether it could go upstream.

## Decisions needed before implementation

1. **Adopt relay mode for Slack (proposed).** Run a clanker-owned Slack connector outside the VMs and a stock Hermes gateway with `RelayAdapter` inside each worker VM. This replaces the current V1_SCOPE wording "reuse Hermes's Slack adapter". Rationale in [section 1](#1-slack-connector-and-gateway-topology). If rejected, the VM-pool architecture needs a different way to move turns from one shared gateway into VMs. Stock Hermes runs agent turns inside the gateway process.
2. **One Hermes context per worker VM.** Each running VM serves exactly one private owner profile or one shared audience profile. Most isolation requirements below assume this.
3. **Disclosed limit, already decided.** During a fill, code in the VM can read the filled value and that site's session. This goes in the access note; it is not built away in v1 ([section 4](#4-vault-and-credential-use)).
4. **Model credentials stay out of the VM (proposed).** See [section 3](#3-worker-vm-sandbox-and-model-access).

## Capability map

| # | Capability | Main delivery | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Slack connector and gateway topology | Clanker + Ext (relay) | Large |
| 2 | Context isolation inside a worker | Config + Patch | Medium |
| 3 | Worker VM sandbox and model access | Config + Clanker | Medium |
| 4 | Vault and credential use | Ext + Patch + Clanker | Large |
| 5 | Access requests and secure input | Patch + Clanker | Large |
| 6 | API key use | Patch + Clanker | Medium |
| 7 | Browser persistence, handoff and revocation | Config + Patch + Clanker | Large |
| 8 | Approvals, consequential actions and publication | Patch + Clanker | Medium |
| 9 | Durable tasks, progress and recovery | Ext + Clanker | Medium |
| 10 | Completion verification | Config + Ext | Small |

---

## 1. Slack connector and gateway topology

### Stock behavior

- The Slack adapter authenticates events, derives workspace (`scope_id`) and sender from the event, and builds correct DM and thread session keys (`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:1749-1822,4471-4588`; `gateway/session.py:673-714`). **Verified.**
- The gateway runs agent turns **in its own process**. A shared Slack gateway cannot hand a turn to a separate VM. **Verified** (the turn path runs in `gateway/run_turn*.py`).
- Known routing traps: broad sender routes override shared-channel routes, unmatched routes fall back to the default profile, MPIMs are labelled `dm`, and approval clicks are checked against bot access rather than the action owner ([Slack audit](verification/audit-slack-notes.md)). **Verified.**
- Hermes ships an **experimental relay mode**. A generic `RelayAdapter` dials out over WebSocket to an external connector that owns the platform connection (`gateway/relay/`, contract in `website/docs/developer-guide/relay-connector-contract.md`). The contract already specifies: **Verified in docs and source**
  - Per-gateway-secret authentication of the WebSocket, with the tenant taken from the connector's own records (§6.1).
  - The connector as the only holder of platform secrets. The gateway holds no Slack token (§6).
  - Per-instance delivery: owner bindings by `(tenant, platform, user_id)`, unbound authors dropped (fail-closed), and a channel owned by at most one instance (§3, §7).
  - Scale-to-zero primitives: `going_idle` / `going_idle_ack`, a durable per-instance buffer with ack-gated replay, and a wake URL the connector pokes (§3.2–3.4).
  - Native interactive prompts (`prompt` op, Slack Block Kit), with the **authentic clicking user** on `prompt_response` (§4).
  - `/stop` interrupts routed to the instance running that session (§5), and media re-hosting so Slack `url_private` credentials never cross the link (§4).
- Nous's reference connector (`NousResearch/gateway-gateway`) is **not public**. Clanker must implement the connector side. **Verified** (repository not resolvable).
- The contract is experimental, validated on Discord and Telegram only. Its discriminator table has no Slack row. **Verified.**

### Why relay

It maps one-to-one onto the architecture board. The connector is the Slack gateway (ingress, routing and dispatch). Instance bindings are the routing and isolation layer. The buffer and wake URL are the queue and wake signal. Each VM's Hermes is a worker. Slack Socket Mode spreads events across connections rather than routing them, so per-VM Slack connections cannot provide per-user routing. **Assumed**; confirm against Slack docs.

### Requirements

- **R1.1 Clanker:** Slack connector service in TypeScript implementing the relay contract, version 1:
  - handshake and `CapabilityDescriptor` for Slack,
  - `inbound`, `outbound`, `outbound_result`, `interrupt` and `going_idle` frames,
  - the `send`, `edit`, `typing`, `prompt`, `send_media`, `react` and `thread_create` ops,
  - media re-hosting,
  - per-gateway secret verification.
- **R1.2 Clanker:** Normalize Slack events into `SessionSource`. `scope_id` = Slack `team_id`. Use `chat_type` `dm` only for 1:1 IMs; label MPIMs `group`. Reject Slack Connect and external-workspace senders unless explicitly allowed.
- **R1.3 Clanker:** A connector-side conformance test asserting that, for each Slack event shape, the session key equals what `gateway/session.py:build_session_key()` would produce. The contract names this function as the oracle.
- **R1.4 Clanker:** The delivery gate. Route a DM to the owner's private instance, and a channel or thread to that channel's audience instance. Drop events from unknown `(team_id, user_id)` or unknown channels, with a short fixed reply. Never fall back to a default instance.
- **R1.5 Clanker:** Owner check on `prompt_response`. For prompts issued by a private instance, accept a press only from that instance's owner; otherwise answer "only <owner> can approve this". Gateway-side approval checks are bot-level and not sufficient ([Slack audit](verification/audit-slack-notes.md), approval finding).
- **R1.6 Config:** Each worker's Hermes runs relay as its only platform. No native Slack adapter or token in the VM. Enrolled with a per-instance secret and wake URL (`hermes gateway enroll --wake-url`, or `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` / `GATEWAY_RELAY_WAKE_URL`).
- **R1.7 Config:** Relay relevance policy: owner DMs always relevant, and channels require an @mention unless listed as free-response (§7.3).
- **R1.8 Patch (only if needed):** Any Slack-specific gap found in `gateway/relay/adapter.py`, for example Block Kit link buttons for access requests ([section 5](#5-access-requests-and-secure-input)). Prefer adding fields to `metadata` that the connector interprets over changing the adapter.

### Acceptance

- Two users DM the bot concurrently. Each reaches only their own instance (checked by instance logs and session keys).
- A user with no binding gets the fixed reply. No instance receives the event.
- An MPIM is classified `group` and does not reach a private instance.
- User B pressing an approval in a thread on A's private prompt is refused by the connector.
- No Slack bot token or signing secret exists anywhere in a worker VM's filesystem or environment.
- `/stop` cancels only the targeted turn.

### Open

- Contract stability: pin connector and gateway to `contract_version` 1 and the pinned Hermes commit.
- Whether `follow_up` and threaded replies cover every Slack reply shape needed. Check during R1.1.

---

## 2. Context isolation inside a worker

### Stock behavior

Profiles separate normal state but are not authorization ([isolation audit](verification/ISOLATION_SOURCE_AUDIT.md)). Within one Hermes process: **Verified**

- `session_search` can open **another profile's** `state.db` when the model names it (`tools/session_search_tool.py:434-444,577-605`).
- Memory is per profile and loaded into every conversation of that profile (`tools/memory_tool.py:38-40`; `agent/system_prompt.py:515-524`).
- The delivery ledger copies final replies into the launch home's `state.db` (`gateway/delivery_ledger.py:171-184,270-283`).
- `send_message` posts to model-chosen destinations without owner approval (`tools/send_message_tool.py:202-275`). The relay egress guard requires destinations to be attested by a session (`gateway/relay/egress.py:485+`), which narrows this on the relay lane. Coverage is **Assumed**.
- The `browser.use_real_profile` CDP cache is process-global (`tools/browser_tool.py:261-266`).

With one context per VM ([decision 2](#decisions-needed-before-implementation)), most of these become harmless: the VM contains only one profile, one ledger and one memory store.

### Requirements

- **R2.1 Config:** One profile per VM, no `gateway.multiplex_profiles`. The profile home is mounted from durable per-context storage ([section 9](#9-durable-tasks-progress-and-recovery)).
- **R2.2 Config / Patch:** No other profile exists in the VM. Additionally make `session_search` refuse any profile other than the current one. That is a one-line guard in `_resolve_profile_db` and protects against misconfiguration.
- **R2.3 Config:** `browser.use_real_profile: false`, `skills.inline_shell: false`, and `security.redact_secrets` left on.
- **R2.4 Config:** Configure an explicit toolset for workers (not the full `hermes-slack` bundle). Keep: browser (`browser_exec` plus vault tools), file tools, `execute_code`, memory, current-profile session search, clarify. Remove: `send_message` ([section 8](#8-approvals-consequential-actions-and-publication)), cron and background jobs unless needed, and any tool that addresses other platforms.
- **R2.5 Config:** Configure the slash-command admin scopes (`allow_admin_from` / `group_allow_admin_from`) so admitted reviewers are not admins (`gateway/slash_access.py:38-48`).
- **R2.6 Clanker:** Audience instances (shared channels) never receive owner credentials, owner browser profiles or owner memory. Work needing a private account goes to the owner's private instance ([section 8](#8-approvals-consequential-actions-and-publication)).

### Acceptance

Re-run [test_profile_boundary.py](verification/probes/test_profile_boundary.py) and [browser_vault_ownership.py](verification/probes/browser_vault_ownership.py) against the worker image. Every cross-context case must now be **denied** or **impossible** (no foreign data present). Today those probes pass because exposure is possible; invert their assertions into acceptance tests.

---

## 3. Worker VM sandbox and model access

### Stock behavior

- `browser_exec` runs arbitrary model-written Python as the Hermes OS user. The only pre-check is URL literals in the code (`tools/browser_use_cli.py:136-139,612-662`). **Verified.**
- Local terminal, file and `execute_code` tools have the OS user's file access ([execution audit](verification/audit-execution-notes.md)). **Verified.**
- Hermes needs a model credential to call the model. The preferred route is ChatGPT/Codex OAuth ([V1_SCOPE.md](V1_SCOPE.md)). Inside the VM, agent code could read that token. **Assumed** (credential lives in the profile home).

### Requirements

- **R3.1 Clanker:** The VM is the sandbox. It contains only: Hermes, Browser Use CLI, Chromium, the context's profile home, its browser profile and workspace files. It holds no vault file or key, Slack token, other context's data, or cloud or pool-manager credentials.
- **R3.2 Clanker:** VM egress: allow the open internet for browsing, but block cloud metadata endpoints and clanker's internal network, except the connector relay endpoint, the trusted handler endpoint and the model proxy.
- **R3.3 Clanker + Config:** Model access through a **model proxy** outside the VM. It holds the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth credential and authenticates each VM by its instance secret. Hermes is configured with a custom OpenAI-compatible base URL and a per-VM token. **Open:** whether the Codex OAuth route can sit behind a proxy (protocol and terms). If it can't, record the token-in-VM exposure as a known limit or use API-key billing behind the proxy.
- **R3.4 Clanker:** Per-VM credentials (relay secret, handler token, model-proxy token) are scoped to that instance and revoked when the VM is rebuilt or reassigned.

### Acceptance

- A test `browser_exec` script that lists the filesystem, environment and reachable internal hosts finds no secrets other than its own instance tokens, and can't reach other VMs or the cloud metadata endpoint.

---

## 4. Vault and credential use

### Stock behavior

Fill logic: **Verified** in `tools/browser_vault_tool.py`.

- `browser_vault_list` returns handles and metadata only, never secrets.
- `browser_vault_fill(handle)` checks the exact origin (pre-check plus an in-page re-check), classifies the field, injects over the supervisor CDP WebSocket and never argv, registers the secret for redaction, and returns counts only.
- `browser_vault_enter_code` mints a TOTP code from the saved key, or prompts the user.
- Card fills require approval (`_confirm_payment_fill` via `request_elicitation_consent`).

Storage: **Verified**

- `VaultStore` at `<profile>/vault/` holds `vault.json.enc` **and** `vault.key` side by side (`agent/vault_store.py:199-201`). Code in the VM can decrypt everything.
- Item types: `login` (optional `otp_secret`), `payment`, `address` (`agent/vault_store.py:35,50`). No API key type.
- Pluggable backends: the `LoginBackend` ABC (`list_items`, `get_meta`, `resolve_password`, `resolve_otp`, `resolve_secret`). The local backend is **always** enabled; 1Password and Bitwarden are optional (`agent/vault_backends/base.py:28-60,125-139`).
- Redaction matches exact substrings only. `browser_exec` output is scrubbed (`tools/browser_use_cli.py:688`), but transformed values are not caught (`agent/redact.py:66-77`).

### Requirements

- **R4.1 Ext + Patch:** A `clanker` vault backend implementing `LoginBackend` by calling the trusted handler over HTTPS with the VM's instance token. Register it in `external_backend_classes()`. **Patch** `enabled_backends()` so the local backend can be disabled by config (`vault.local.enabled: false`).
- **R4.2 Config:** Workers run with the local, 1Password and Bitwarden backends disabled. Only the `clanker` backend is active. No `vault.key` ever exists in the VM.
- **R4.3 Clanker:** The trusted handler stores secrets encrypted, with keys outside every VM. Entries are keyed by `(tenant, owner, kind, label)` with bound origins. It supports:
  - `list(context)`: metadata for the calling instance's owner only.
  - `resolve(handle, origin)`: releases one secret only if the handle belongs to the instance's owner, the origin matches, and the instance has an active task. Every release is logged without values.
  - `resolve_otp(handle, origin)`: computes the TOTP code **in the handler**, so the setup key never enters the VM. Reuse Hermes's `totp_now` / `normalize_otp_secret` logic (port to TypeScript or run as a small Python sidecar in the handler).
- **R4.4 Ext:** Audience instances get a backend that lists nothing ([R2.6](#2-context-isolation-inside-a-worker)).
- **R4.5 Patch:** Add an `api_key` item type to the backend surface: metadata visible, never fillable into pages by default, and used through [section 6](#6-api-key-use).
- **R4.6 Clanker:** Card policy. Store number, expiry and CVV only if the owner chooses "save card". The default is a single-use card request that the handler deletes after one fill. Every card fill needs owner approval through the owner-checked prompt ([R1.5](#1-slack-connector-and-gateway-topology)).
- **R4.7 Docs:** Access-note entry for the disclosed fill-time limit ([decision 3](#decisions-needed-before-implementation)).

### Acceptance

- A login saved through the web form fills on the exact origin in a fresh VM and is refused on any other origin.
- A TOTP-protected test account logs in with no user prompt. The setup key is not found anywhere in the VM.
- Instance B can't list or resolve instance A's handles (handler returns 403). The handler log shows the attempt.
- Deleting an entry makes the next `resolve` fail ([section 7](#7-browser-persistence-handoff-and-revocation) covers sessions).

---

## 5. Access requests and secure input

### Stock behavior

- `browser_vault_save_login`, `browser_vault_unlock` and the user-prompt path of `browser_vault_enter_code` need prompt callbacks. These exist in CLI, TUI and Desktop, but **the messaging gateway never registers them**, so in Slack these tools return `prompt_unavailable` ([browser audit](verification/audit-browser-notes.md), "Related secure input finding"). **Verified.**
- Hermes has no asynchronous "request access, then resume" flow. **Verified.**

### Requirements

Modeled on Instinct's vault-fill request (fixed per-type schemas; the agent chooses only the type, title and fields).

- **R5.1 Patch:** New tool `vault_request_access(kind, label, site, fields?, reason)`:
  - `kind` is one of `login`, `payment`, `address`, `api_key`.
  - `fields` is a subset of that kind's schema. The login schema is `username`, `password` and optional `totp` setup key.
  - It calls the handler and returns `{request_id, status: "waiting_for_owner"}`. It never returns the link.
  - The agent then ends its turn with a short status message.
  - In clanker mode, `browser_vault_save_login` delegates to this tool, and the user-prompt branch of `browser_vault_enter_code` returns guidance to request a TOTP key or use the browser handoff ([section 7](#7-browser-persistence-handoff-and-revocation)).
- **R5.2 Clanker:** The handler validates the request:
  - the owner is the calling instance's owner;
  - the kind exists and the fields belong to it, with unknown keys rejected;
  - for logins, `site` must equal the current page's origin as reported by the fill path, not just model text;
  - it creates a single-use token that expires in about 30 minutes.
- **R5.3 Clanker:** The handler, not the worker, asks the connector to DM the owner a Block Kit card with a "Connect <label>" button. The link never enters model context or the worker's logs.
- **R5.4 Clanker:** Vault web app:
  - Sign in with Slack (OIDC), with state, nonce and signature checks, and `team_id` + `user_id` matched to the request's owner.
  - Screens for wrong account, expired or used link, and not found.
  - One fixed form per kind, with correct labels ("API key", not "Password"), secret fields masked with a reveal toggle, and typed values kept in the tab if saving fails.
  - Submission goes straight to the handler.
- **R5.5 Clanker:** On a durable save, the handler marks the request used and asks the connector to inject a synthetic inbound event into the owner's instance session: "Access saved: <label> (<kind>, <origin>)". This carries metadata only. It wakes the instance if suspended ([section 9](#9-durable-tasks-progress-and-recovery)). The success page shows "Saved. clanker is continuing" with a deep link back to the Slack conversation.
- **R5.6 Clanker:** Vault management page (same app): list entries by metadata, delete, and replace. Deleting triggers [R7.4](#7-browser-persistence-handoff-and-revocation). Viewing saved values is out of scope for v1.

### Acceptance

- From Slack: the agent hits a login page, the owner gets a DM card, saves the form, and the task continues in the same thread without a new message from the user.
- The link opened by another Slack user shows "wrong account". A reused link shows "no longer works". A tampered `fields` list is rejected.
- No secret, link or token appears in Slack messages, model inputs, the queue, connector logs or worker logs (grep a full run's logs and transcripts for canary values).

---

## 6. API key use

### Stock behavior

There is no API key item type and no tool that authenticates an HTTP request from the vault. The agent's only path to an API would be to see the key. **Verified.**

### Requirements

- **R6.1 Patch:** New tool `vault_http_request(handle, method, url, headers?, json?, body?)`. The worker forwards it to the handler and never resolves the key itself.
- **R6.2 Clanker:** The handler:
  - checks that the handle belongs to the owner and that the URL's origin is in the item's bound origins, with exact matching (e.g. `https://openrouter.ai`);
  - injects the key into the item's auth scheme (`Authorization: Bearer` by default; header name configurable per item);
  - sends the request, with timeouts and a response size cap;
  - scrubs the key from the response;
  - returns status, headers (minus `set-cookie`) and body.
- **R6.3 Clanker:** For binary results (e.g. a generated video), the handler can store the response as an artifact and return a reference the worker can download, or send it to the owner via the connector's `send_media`.
- **R6.4 Config / prompt:** Agent guidance for the request, poll and download pattern (as Instinct does for OpenRouter video), with the cost stated up front and a spend cap confirmed with the owner before the first billable call.

### Acceptance

- The assignment's OpenRouter task completes end to end. The key never appears in the VM, model inputs or logs.
- A `vault_http_request` to any non-bound origin with an OpenRouter handle is refused.

---

## 7. Browser persistence, handoff and revocation

### Stock behavior

- Browser Use with local Chromium is the selected stack (`browser.cloud_provider: local`, `backend: browser-use`) ([V1_SCOPE.md](V1_SCOPE.md)). Default local sessions are temporary. **Verified** (`tools/browser_tool_session.py:243-271`).
- Named Browser Use sessions are keyed by `(profile, session name)` (`tools/browser_use_cli.py:364-376`). This is harmless with one context per VM.
- Hermes has a human-takeover lease for its Bot Desktop browser (`tools/bot_desktop/lease.py`, `HumanHasControl`), which the vault fill honors (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:147-157`). The same package includes `rfb_filter.py`, which suggests an existing VNC (RFB) viewing path. Whether either works for a remote handoff from a worker VM is **Open**. Investigate before building R7.2 from scratch.
- Nothing streams the browser to a remote human, and removing a vault entry does not touch browser cookies. **Verified.**

### Requirements

- **R7.1 Config + Clanker:** A persistent Chromium profile per context (user-data dir in durable storage), reused across tasks and VM replacement. Verify that `browser_exec` and the vault supervisor attach to the same persistent browser. A dedicated Chromium connected through CDP is the documented option. **Open:** the exact config to validate.
- **R7.2 Clanker:** Live browser handoff for SMS, email or phone OTP, CAPTCHAs, passkeys and the "log in yourself" access option:
  - The agent calls a `request_handoff(reason)` tool (**Patch**, small). The handler DMs the owner a link through the connector.
  - The link opens a Sign-in-with-Slack-protected viewer streaming the VM's Chromium (CDP `Page.startScreencast` plus input relay, or noVNC), proxied through the trusted side.
  - While the human has control the agent must not act. Reuse or mirror the Bot Desktop lease so fills and `browser_exec` refuse during takeover.
  - "Done" in the viewer returns control and injects a resume event (as in R5.5).
- **R7.3 Config / prompt:** The agent prefers handoff over asking for codes in chat, and never asks for secrets in Slack.
- **R7.4 Clanker:** Revocation. When the owner deletes a vault entry or chooses "Disconnect <site>", the handler:
  1. deletes the secret;
  2. records a revocation for that origin;
  3. clears that origin's cookies and storage in the owner's persistent browser profile, immediately if the instance is live (via a privileged CDP call outside agent code), otherwise when the profile is next mounted;
  4. refuses any later `resolve` for it.
- **R7.5 Docs:** Access-note entry: cookies for the site in use are reachable by code in the VM during a task (same limit as decision 3).

### Acceptance

- Log in once, then complete a second task on the same site in a **new VM** without re-entering credentials.
- An SMS-OTP site such as Swiggy completes through the handoff viewer. The agent resumes after "Done".
- After "Disconnect Gmail", a new task finds Gmail logged out and has no saved login.

---

## 8. Approvals, consequential actions and publication

### Stock behavior

- Approvals use gateway prompts. On relay these become `prompt` ops, and the press carries the authentic clicker, but gateway authorization is bot-level, not owner-level ([Slack audit](verification/audit-slack-notes.md)). **Verified.**
- `send_message` can publish anywhere the bot can post. **Verified.**

### Requirements

- **R8.1 Clanker:** The owner check on prompt presses ([R1.5](#1-slack-connector-and-gateway-topology)) covers every approval kind: tool approvals, card fills, purchases and sends.
- **R8.2 Config / prompt:** The agent asks for concrete confirmation before purchases, external messages, publication and deletion, with the exact details (item, amount, recipient). Changed details need fresh confirmation. **Open:** whether a Hermes approval mechanism can enforce this for browser actions, or whether it stays a prompt-level rule plus card-fill enforcement. Investigate `tools/approval_prompt.py`.
- **R8.3 Config:** Remove `send_message` from worker toolsets. Instances reply only to their own conversation through the normal reply path.
- **R8.4 Patch + Clanker:** New tool `propose_share(content, destination)` for private instances. The connector DMs the owner a preview with Approve / Decline buttons, owner-checked. When approved, the connector posts the exact approved content to the destination. Edited content needs a new approval. The audience instance receives the shared message as ordinary channel content, with no access to the source.
- **R8.5 Clanker:** A shared-thread request that needs a private account. The audience instance tells the requester it will continue privately. The connector creates or uses the owner's DM session and injects the task there, then results come back through R8.4.

### Acceptance

- Another user can't approve a card fill or a share for someone else's private task.
- A private result appears in a channel only after the owner approves that exact text.

---

## 9. Durable tasks, progress and recovery

### Stock behavior

- Conversation and tool history persists in the profile's `state.db`. The delivery ledger records replies for recovery (`gateway/delivery_ledger.py`). **Verified.**
- The relay buffers inbound for a suspended instance, replays it with ack gating, and pokes the wake URL (contract §3.2–3.4). Suspend and idle behavior is left to the operator. **Verified** (docs).
- Whether an interrupted turn (VM lost mid-task) resumes is **Open**. Assume it does not.

### Requirements

- **R9.1 Clanker:** VM pool manager: wake URL endpoint, start or resume the context's VM, mount its profile home and browser profile, and enforce one live VM per context. It honors contract §3.4: register the wake URL before any suspend, suspend only after `going_idle_ack`, and treat suspended as healthy.
- **R9.2 Clanker:** Durable per-context storage for the profile home and browser profile. Snapshot on suspend and restore on start. Rebuild a VM from the image before giving it to a different context.
- **R9.3 Clanker:** Turn-level recovery. The connector records each inbound task as `accepted`, `running` or `done`, using the reply as the completion signal. If an instance dies with a turn `running`, the connector re-delivers that inbound to the replacement with a note: "Previous attempt was interrupted; check the current state before repeating any action." This is the minimum needed so consequential steps aren't blindly replayed.
- **R9.4 Config / prompt:** Brief progress updates for long tasks, via edit or `typing`. One acknowledgement within a few seconds of the request.
- **R9.5 Clanker:** Cancellation: `/stop` maps to the relay interrupt ([section 1](#1-slack-connector-and-gateway-topology)). Bounded execution: a per-task wall-clock limit in the connector.

### Acceptance

- Kill a VM mid-task. A replacement resumes the same conversation and finishes without repeating a completed purchase or send.
- Suspend an idle instance, then send a DM. It wakes and answers with history intact.

---

## 10. Completion verification

### Requirements

- **R10.1 Config / prompt:** Before reporting done, the agent checks the outcome on the site itself, for example the order confirmation page, the deployment URL returning 200, or the downloaded artifact opening. Its final message states what it checked.
- **R10.2 Ext (optional):** A post-turn hook flags final messages that claim completion without a verification step in that turn, for evaluation logs only.

### Acceptance

- Across the release evidence tasks, every "done" message names a checked result, and spot checks confirm it.

---

## Patch register

| ID | File (pinned) | Change | Section | Upstreamable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | `tools/session_search_tool.py` | Refuse non-current profiles when a config flag is set | 2 | Likely (as an option) |
| P2 | `agent/vault_backends/base.py` | Optional local backend; register the `clanker` backend | 4 | Likely (generic remote backend) |
| P3 | `agent/vault_backends/` + `agent/vault_store.py` | `api_key` item type | 4, 6 | Possibly |
| P4 | `tools/browser_vault_tool.py` | `vault_request_access`; clanker-mode save and code-prompt behavior | 5 | Possibly (async access requests) |
| P5 | new `tools/vault_http_tool.py` | `vault_http_request` | 6 | Possibly |
| P6 | new tool | `request_handoff` | 7 | Possibly |
| P7 | new tool | `propose_share` | 8 | Unlikely (clanker-specific) |
| P8 | `gateway/relay/adapter.py` | Only if the Slack lane needs it (R1.8) | 1 | Yes |

Keep patches as separate commits on a `clanker` branch of the pinned commit, each with tests next to the upstream ones. Prefer plugins where a hook suffices.

## Suggested build order

1. **Relay spike (de-risks decision 1).** A minimal connector: Slack DM in, one VM's Hermes on relay, reply out. Then add a `prompt` round trip with an owner check.
2. **Worker image and isolation config (sections 2 and 3).** Flip the existing probes into acceptance tests.
3. **Vault backend and handler (section 4)**, then **access requests and the web app (section 5)**. This gives the first complete credential flow.
4. **Persistent browser and revocation (section 7, R7.1 and R7.4)**, then **API key use (section 6)**.
5. **Handoff viewer (R7.2)**, **approvals and sharing (section 8)**, and **recovery (section 9)**.
6. Run the assignment's example prompt end to end (Gmail sign-in to Vercel, the OpenRouter video, the Swiggy reorder) as the release check.

deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:31:Every directory component created inside the private staging root is explicitly set to 0700 through directory file descriptors, including intermediate directories under a normal 022 umask. Publication uses the platform's atomic no-replace primitive: macOS `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` or Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. A competing destination is preserved even when its creator ignores the advisory lock. An unavailable primitive, unsupported platform, or unsupported filesystem causes explicit refusal, with no check-then-rename fallback. Source/destination parent directories must still be trusted and stable; this does not defend against a hostile process replacing ancestors. The native macOS path was exercised locally; the Linux path requires its own runtime check before deployment. References: [Apple rename manual](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/man/man2/rename.2), [Apple flag definitions](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/stdio.h), [Linux rename manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat2.2.html), [Linux flag definitions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/fs.h).
deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:33:Limits are deliberately small for the fixture: 1,024 files/pending directory entries, 64 MiB aggregate payload, 1 MiB manifest, a bounded uncompressed archive, and a cooperative 20-second processing deadline. These limits are not a measured production browser-profile size. Slow filesystem calls are not subject to a hard preemptive wall-clock deadline. No compression, extraction shell command, cloud client, subprocess, or network call is used.

deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:31:Every directory component created inside the private staging root is explicitly set to 0700 through directory file descriptors, including intermediate directories under a normal 022 umask. Publication uses the platform's atomic no-replace primitive: macOS `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` or Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. A competing destination is preserved even when its creator ignores the advisory lock. An unavailable primitive, unsupported platform, or unsupported filesystem causes explicit refusal, with no check-then-rename fallback. Source/destination parent directories must still be trusted and stable; this does not defend against a hostile process replacing ancestors. The native macOS path was exercised locally; the Linux path requires its own runtime check before deployment. References: [Apple rename manual](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/man/man2/rename.2), [Apple flag definitions](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/stdio.h), [Linux rename manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat2.2.html), [Linux flag definitions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/fs.h).
deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:33:Limits are deliberately small for the fixture: 1,024 files/pending directory entries, 64 MiB aggregate payload, 1 MiB manifest, a bounded uncompressed archive, and a cooperative 20-second processing deadline. These limits are not a measured production browser-profile size. Slow filesystem calls are not subject to a hard preemptive wall-clock deadline. No compression, extraction shell command, cloud client, subprocess, or network call is used.

deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:10:.local/hermes-lab/venv/bin/python -B deployment/cloudflare/persistence/test_snapshot_fixture.py
deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:31:Every directory component created inside the private staging root is explicitly set to 0700 through directory file descriptors, including intermediate directories under a normal 022 umask. Publication uses the platform's atomic no-replace primitive: macOS `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` or Linux `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`. A competing destination is preserved even when its creator ignores the advisory lock. An unavailable primitive, unsupported platform, or unsupported filesystem causes explicit refusal, with no check-then-rename fallback. Source/destination parent directories must still be trusted and stable; this does not defend against a hostile process replacing ancestors. The native macOS path was exercised locally; the Linux path requires its own runtime check before deployment. References: [Apple rename manual](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/man/man2/rename.2), [Apple flag definitions](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/stdio.h), [Linux rename manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/renameat2.2.html), [Linux flag definitions](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/uapi/linux/fs.h).
deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:33:Limits are deliberately small for the fixture: 1,024 files/pending directory entries, 64 MiB aggregate payload, 1 MiB manifest, a bounded uncompressed archive, and a cooperative 20-second processing deadline. These limits are not a measured production browser-profile size. Slow filesystem calls are not subject to a hard preemptive wall-clock deadline. No compression, extraction shell command, cloud client, subprocess, or network call is used.

deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:49:## Three-owner runtime boundary
deployment/cloudflare/persistence/README.md:51:The trusted Slack ingress resolves verified workspace/user identifiers to owner IDs. Up to three isolated full Hermes runtimes can be leased simultaneously. Each receives only its owner's home, browser state, workspace files, and authorized credentials. A shared Slack channel does not authorize access to another owner's checkpoint. Do not select checkpoints from prompt text, display names, arbitrary object keys, or caller-chosen container names.

## 1. Routing, privacy and collaboration

Hermes documents sender/workspace routing, admission controls and shared thread sessions. However, unmatched routes fall through to the default/active profile. Sender-specific routes outrank location-only routes, so a broad private-user route can also capture that person's shared-channel messages. Admission and routing need separate configuration. [Profile routing documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways/#routing-shared-bot-chats-to-profiles-profile_routes)

Profiles separate stored state but provide no filesystem sandbox. Local terminal execution retains the operating-system user's access, including outside the profile directory. Changing the working directory cannot enforce ownership. [Profile isolation limits](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/profiles/#profiles-vs-workspaces-vs-sandboxing)

Memory is also a profile-level resource: persistent memory files enter new sessions' prompts. Private and shared conversations using one profile therefore need more than separate transcripts. Shared threads support collaboration, and `/stop` can affect another admitted participant's run in the same room/thread. Private account work needs a private execution context. [Memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory/), [session behavior](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#shared-vs-isolated-group-sessions)

**Specific source finding:** `session_search` exposes a model-selected `profile`. Its dispatch also accepts a profile embedded in a session reference, then opens the named profile's database. The inspected resolution/dispatch functions do not check the requester's ownership. An outer tool restriction could change the deployed result; the full gateway call graph was not audited. Test or constrain this path before enabling it for reviewers. [Database resolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L434), [dispatch](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L577), [model-visible schema and registration](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/tools/session_search_tool.py#L769)

Hermes's documented command approval modes govern dangerous shell commands. They do not establish confirmation for every consequential website action or approval to publish private results. # Cloudflare account access check

Date: 2026-10-04. **Read-only; no resources, billing changes, tokens, or deployments created.** Account email and identifier are omitted from this shareable evidence.

The installed Cloudflare plugin uses the official OAuth MCP endpoint, `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp`. An authenticated Codex app-server MCP client performed direct API GET requests without an LLM request. The server reported connected/OAuth; account listing returned one account. Raw responses remain in the ignored local lab directory and were not copied into this document.

| GET endpoint under the selected account | Observed result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workers/account-settings` | HTTP 200; `default_usage_model=standard` | Settings readable; this field is not proof of the billing plan. |
| `workers/scripts` | HTTP 200; empty list | No existing Workers returned. |
| `workers/durable_objects/namespaces` | HTTP 200; total count 0 | No existing Durable Object namespaces. |
| `workers/subdomain` | HTTP 200; a configured subdomain | Workers subdomain configuration is readable. |
| `containers/applications` | API error 1000: no Containers access; Workers Paid upgrade required | This account lacks Containers entitlement. Application count is unknown because listing was denied. |
| `r2/buckets` | API error 10042: enable R2 through the dashboard | R2 is not enabled. No bucket was created. |
| `subscriptions` | API error 10000: authentication error | Exact subscription names cannot be established with this OAuth access. |

The earlier CLI-assisted inspection failed at its model request. The later direct MCP inspection above succeeded for the listed APIs; that earlier failure does not establish a problem with Hermes's separately authorized model account. Read access does not prove future deployment/write permissions.

Containers' paid gate conflicts with the user's current free-only scope. No upgrade or alternative hosting provider was selected. See the [preflight](../CLOUDFLARE_PREFLIGHT.md) for deployment and recovery gaps.

# Native profile-memory verification — 4 October 2026

**Passed:** two real users sent the same Slack request to the same `@clanker`. One stock Hermes gateway, **PID 29828**, loaded each routed profile's native memory into a fresh model context and returned exactly that profile's expected value. Both requests offered **zero tools**. Run: `20261004T153240Z`; Hermes **0.21.5**, commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`.

1. **Seed different persistent state.** The operator used stock `MemoryStore.add` to save one random synthetic value in each profile's `memories/MEMORY.md`, then reopened the store ([setup source](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/poc_profile_context/prepare_run.py:89)). The shared `SOUL.md` was left unchanged; both saved baselines have SHA-256 `568bbe0e664dd5ae957bbd9eeb1cac22fb9680ba7883cd509cecccd9299b6e6b`. Expected values remain in the [private oracle](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/oracle.private.json); this report contains only their hashes.

2. **Ask the identical question from two actual users.** `U0C684PHZ5H` and `U0C688SF7DZ` each requested exactly the remembered dummy verification token, with nothing else. The complete submitted texts were identical and contained neither expected value. [Slack server records](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/submitted-messages.json) confirm both senders, workspace `T0C6J1XCDE0`, channel `C0C6J277ZNG`, and serialized bot mention `U0C5Z1ZQHQX`. [A thread](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791128100320699) · [B thread](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791128100110029).

3. **Inspect the actual prepared requests.** A used `owner-a-public` / session `20261004_210502_74c47f9e`; B used `owner-b-public` / session `20261004_210502_e263ecba`. Each made one `codex_responses` request. [A receipt](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/A-events.jsonl:4) and [B receipt](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/B-events.jsonl:4) show the exact native-memory text in the system prompt, only the respective marker hash, and **zero agent and outbound tool schemas**. Stock [profile scoping](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/gateway/run.py:1810), [memory loading](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/agent/agent_init.py:1259), [prompt assembly](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/agent/system_prompt.py:515), and [request observer](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/upstream/agent/turn_api_request.py:42) establish the path; custom hooks only recorded evidence.

4. **Compare complete replies and execution.** The [independent verifier](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/poc_profile_context/verify_live.py) passed again against saved evidence. Both complete final replies exactly equaled their own oracle value, with no other profile's value: A hash `d32687da9ad5c0a6ac860a798e9d305aa43369f25afc50e3f723012d7cadd49b`; B hash `9506bb63491aa18f43cadbda0c0679cddcbcfcd0833e6fc22c27e720e981b7ff`. [A answer](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791128109391549) · [B answer](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791128109740239). Each thread's separate stock no-home-channel notice was excluded from final-answer evaluation. [Verification results](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/behavioral-verification.json) and [gateway state](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/gateway-state-active.json) agree on PID **29828**, two active agents and **4.533321708 seconds** of overlapping task execution.

5. **Keep the conclusion bounded.** This demonstrates behavioral recall from operator-seeded, profile-local persistent files in two fresh sessions. It does **not** demonstrate agent learning, agent-written durability across restart, automatic reviewer onboarding, unrestricted-tool authorization or production isolation. Both dummy answers were intentionally posted in the shared test channel, so this is not a test of private result delivery. No browser task was performed. The [POC files were restored](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/poc-restored.json), and the [original gateway resumed as PID 30278](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/primary-restored.json), with original-file hashes matching and all three existing browser endpoints healthy.

The [source manifest](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/profile-context-poc/evidence/source-hash-manifest.json) records the clean upstream pin and SHA-256 hashes for 14 reviewed source files; all 14 were independently rechecked. Input hashes are recorded in the behavioral verification report. [Detailed source audit](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/poc_profile_context/SOURCE_AUDIT.md).

The [30.5-second walkthrough](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-profile-memory-2026-10-04/verification.mp4) is captioned and silent. # Two-user parallel public-browser verification — 4 October 2026

**Execution and narrated video verified.** Two actual Slack members supplied different harmless MDN research requests. A temporary polling dispatcher ran those requests in two separate stock Hermes `AIAgent` processes. The latest successful rerun completed both tasks correctly, with overlapping task intervals and interleaved navigation calls. Earlier runs separately measured overlapping browser-tool calls.

[Watch the 67.67-second narrated video](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/clanker-two-user-verification-narrated.mp4). It contains original Slack request footage, UTC-aligned actual worker recordings at 1x, an evidence/scope card, and ElevenLabs Hinglish narration. Worker footage is explicitly labeled as a rerun of the same verified requests. Full video/audio decoding and visual review passed; all six method pages are visible.

This is evidence for the temporary dispatcher and separate-process test architecture. It is not acceptance evidence for the existing shared Slack gateway, an OS sandbox, or complete tenant authorization.

1. **The requests came from two real Slack identities.** Saved Slack API records bind account A (`U0C684PHZ5H`) and account B (`U0C688SF7DZ`) to distinct top-level messages in workspace `T0C6J1XCDE0`, channel `C0C6J277ZNG` (`clanker-test`). Sender IDs and exact request text match the prepared test plan. [Account A request](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791122659149849) · [Account B request](https://clanker-global.slack.com/archives/C0C6J277ZNG/p1791122659695169). This audit checked the saved API records; the video shows the original posted requests, while the API evidence establishes their senders and timestamps.

2. **Each request had a separate restricted worker.** The pinned Hermes commit was `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`. Each worker used a fresh Hermes home/workspace, a different process, and a different dedicated Chromium endpoint. The dedicated public-worker Chromium processes were reused across recording retries and preflights; fresh Hermes homes do not imply fresh or empty browser state on each rerun. No private Slack browser state was supplied to these workers. The exact offered tools were `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_scroll`, and `browser_back`. No session search, vault, terminal, file, delegation, or typing tools were offered. Explicit navigation was restricted to `developer.mozilla.org`; that guard is not a redirect-aware network firewall. The dispatcher polled authenticated Slack history rather than opening a competing Socket Mode connection.

3. **The browser work overlapped.** Task intervals run from `task_start` to `task_result`; tool intervals run from matched `tool_start` to `tool_complete`. Calculations use the same host's recorded monotonic clock. Preparation, model initialization, Slack waiting, cleanup, and post-result recording holds are excluded. Browser-tool overlap means that browser navigation calls were simultaneously in flight; it does not measure CPU or network utilization.

| Run | Task overlap | Browser-tool overlap | Overlapping tool intervals | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `parallel-20261004T140346Z` | N/A — no task starts in saved logs | 0 s observed | 0 | Initial dispatcher preparation failed |
| `parallel-20261004T140540Z` | 90.225843 s | 31.595991584 s | 3 | Both workers completed; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |
| `parallel-20261004T141401Z` | N/A — neither task started | 0 s observed | 0 | Preparation could not identify one recording target |
| `parallel-20261004T141510Z` | 41.681174084 s | 4.021236625 s | 1 | Both workers completed; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |
| `parallel-20261004T142615Z` | N/A — neither task started | 0 s observed | 0 | Recorder gate timed out; preparation failed before task execution |
| `parallel-20261004T143238Z` | 23.281013042 s | 0 s | 0 | Concurrent tasks with interleaved navigation; 6/6 required pages; 12/12 facts correct |

The `parallel-20261004T141510Z` run deliberately replayed the **same original authenticated Slack messages**; it was not a second pair of user submissions. Its 10-second post-result recording hold for each worker is excluded. The overlapping browser calls in that run were OPTIONS and DELETE, from 19:45:47.684 to 19:45:51.705 IST.

The `parallel-20261004T142615Z` attempt prepared both real browser targets, but neither received the recorder-ready acknowledgment within 150 seconds. Both exited with `TimeoutError` at approximately 19:58:49 IST before `task_start`; no model-driven browsing or answer evaluation occurred. This is a recording/preparation failure, not a measured browser-task failure. Earlier successful execution results remain separate from this unsuccessful capture attempt.

The final `parallel-20261004T143238Z` attempt again replayed the original authenticated messages. Its task intervals overlap from 20:02:51.448 to 20:03:14.729 IST, but its six short navigation calls are interleaved: **zero simultaneous in-flight browser-tool overlap was measured in this run**. Its 23.281013042-second task overlap excludes blank-tab prewarming, recorder-gate waiting, and both 10-second post-result holds. Earlier positive tool-overlap measurements must not be substituted for this run's zero measurement.

4. **The answers matched independent page evidence.** Account A requested GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS; account B requested POST, PUT, and DELETE. Each worker successfully navigated all three required official pages. All twelve Safe/Idempotent values matched both the returned browser snapshots and a separate HTTPS fetch/table parser. The oracle was fetched during the first run and reused for the rerun. Responses used three source-linked bullets rather than the requested table.

| Method | Safe | Idempotent | Official source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | Yes | Yes | [MDN GET](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/GET) |
| HEAD | Yes | Yes | [MDN HEAD](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/HEAD) |
| OPTIONS | Yes | Yes | [MDN OPTIONS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/OPTIONS) |
| POST | No | No | [MDN POST](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/POST) |
| PUT | No | Yes | [MDN PUT](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/PUT) |
| DELETE | No | Yes | [MDN DELETE](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Methods/DELETE) |

5. **The tested privacy boundary was narrow.** Before execution, distinct dummy cookie values remained in their respective fresh worker browsers. This establishes that preflight cookie separation check only; it was not repeated as a post-run attack test. Both workers still run under the same OS user. Private-data authorization, hostile cross-worker access, credential revocation, private artifact sharing, stock shared-gateway behavior, hosted deployment, restart recovery, and three-user capacity remain unverified. The earlier unrestricted `session_search` finding is not resolved by this experiment.

Reviewable local evidence:

- [Latest successful rerun report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/verification-report.json), [first-run report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T140540Z/verification-report.json), and [earlier rerun report](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T141510Z/verification-report.json), including exact intervals, checked facts, absolute artifact paths, and SHA-256 hashes.
- [Latest account A events](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/A-events.jsonl) and [account B events](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/B-events.jsonl).
- [Verified actual Slack messages](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/verified-messages.json) and [latest worker results](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T143238Z/results.json).
- [Independent public-page oracle](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/independent-oracle.json) and [dummy-cookie preflight](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/browser-isolation-preflight.json).
- [Recorder-gate preparation failure audit](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/two-user-recording/runs/parallel-20261004T142615Z/verification-report.json), recording the missing task starts, zero task-tool calls, and recorder-gate timeout.

Final artifact verification: [video/audio QA and SHA-256](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/final-verification.json), [capture continuity and six page frames](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final-capture-2/capture-review.json), and [edit timing manifest](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-two-user-2026-10-04/final/edit-manifest.json). The final MP4 is 1920×1080 H.264 with AAC narration, 67.666667 seconds. Original browser capture is 5 fps; delivery is 30 fps with duplicate frames, without speeding up execution. Track alignment uses recorded UTC capture clocks within the source frame resolution. All three existing browser endpoints remained reachable after recording.

Earlier recording failures remain preserved separately. The first worker capture used incorrect tabs and failed encoder shutdown; the next recorded execution had a roughly 28-second capture gap and is not used as continuous execution evidence. The successful capture uses yyoreel’s screencast path, explicit stream dimensions, a six-second warmup, and activation of the owned public tabs before capturing. Narration was generated with ElevenLabs (Tara, `eleven_multilingual_v2`); the complete 56.285-second take is retained, with a 10.856-second quiet viewing interval inserted before the results commentary. No private data authorization or stock shared-gateway acceptance is established by the video.

# clanker local Hermes baseline

Start with **unmodified upstream Hermes**, cloned locally and pinned. A remote fork becomes useful only if a reproduced gap requires an upstream patch. The project directory stays named `yyot`; the product is **clanker**.

## State

The stock CLI is installed and starts locally. [Live Slack owner-command connectivity passes](evidence/2026-10-03-slack-connectivity.md), and fresh owner OAuth plus [tool-free CLI, owner Slack DM and channel mention inference pass](evidence/2026-10-03-model-slack-smoke.md). No browser task, deployment or complete V1 acceptance has been completed. Initial upstream test results are recorded separately below; they do not establish clanker's privacy contract.

| Component | Baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [NousResearch/hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) |
| Release | `v2026.9.24`, Hermes `0.21.5` |
| Commit | `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f` |
| Interpreter | Python `3.13.13` |
| Dependency selection | Committed `uv.lock`, `slack` and `dev` extras |
| Installer used | uv `0.11.16` |
| Checkout | `.local/hermes-lab/upstream` |
| Environment | `.local/hermes-lab/venv` |
| State and credentials | `.local/hermes-lab/home` |
| Working directory | `.local/hermes-lab/workspace` |
| Launcher | `scripts/hermes-lab` |

All lab files are Git-ignored. The existing globally installed Hermes is separate and was not upgraded. The pinned release supports Python 3.11–3.13; moving website instructions for newer releases must not replace its setup instructions.

## Reproduce a fresh installation

Run from the project root with Git and uv available:

```sh
mkdir -p .local/hermes-lab
git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch v2026.9.24 \
  https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git .local/hermes-lab/upstream
test "$(git -C .local/hermes-lab/upstream rev-parse HEAD)" = \
  f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f
```

Then install the committed dependency selection into its dedicated environment:

```sh
(
  cd .local/hermes-lab/upstream
  UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$PWD/../venv" \
    uv sync --locked --python 3.13.13 --extra slack --extra dev
)
ln -s ../venv .local/hermes-lab/upstream/.venv
scripts/hermes-lab --version
```

The symlink ensures the upstream test runner selects this environment before any existing personal Hermes installation. These are fresh-install commands; reuse an existing matching checkout/environment instead of cloning over it. The release commit and lockfile are the baseline; no Hermes update command should run during a recorded experiment.

## Local state separation

The launcher copies [the initial configuration](hermes/config.yaml) only when the lab has no configuration. It clears inherited credentials/session variables, disables automatic adoption of existing Codex/Claude logins, disables lazy dependency installation, selects dedicated gateway-lock and managed-policy directories, and creates a mode-600 `.env` for deliberate lab credentials. It rejects a fallback `.env` in the upstream checkout and preserves existing lab settings on subsequent runs.

**This is configuration separation, not an OS security boundary.** The process keeps the current user's filesystem permissions. Do not use real private accounts for the two-user boundary tests. A functioning container/VM or another verified execution boundary is needed before accepting runtime isolation. Docker's CLI exists on this machine, but its daemon was unavailable at setup time.

Keep `auth.adopt_external_logins: false` after setup. Do not use `--safe-mode` or `--ignore-user-config` in this baseline: those switches discard user configuration. Do not invoke explicit credential import or service installation as part of a routing test. The adoption setting covers Codex/Claude, not every provider's authentication path; authentication/model setup must be deliberately reviewed before use. The owner manually authorized fresh `openai-codex` OAuth for the local smoke. Credentials remain in ignored lab `auth.json` (mode `0600`, home directory `0700`); reviewer/hosted funding compatibility and billing treatment remain unverified.

## Initial checks

The launcher successfully ran `--help`, `--version`, and `gateway --help`. These commands did not start a gateway or make an inference request.

Run the targeted upstream routing checks with its canonical runner:

```sh
(
  cd .local/hermes-lab/upstream
  scripts/run_tests.sh -j 4 \
    tests/gateway/test_profile_routing.py \
    tests/gateway/test_slack_channel_session_scope.py \
    tests/gateway/test_slack_bot_auth_bypass.py \
    tests/gateway/test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py
)
```

The runner clears credential variables and uses a separate process for each test file. Upstream fixtures supply temporary state and synthetic events. These checks cover existing routing/session behavior and selected admission regressions; they do not exercise real Slack, model-driven tools, cross-owner filesystem enforcement, or hosted recovery.

**Result on 2026-10-03: 47 passed, 0 failed across four files; runner exit code 0.** The profile-routing file contributed 18 tests, Slack channel session scope 4, Slack bot admission 2, and profile database scope 23. Runner time was 9.7 seconds, excluding its initial bytecode compilation. See [the captured output](evidence/2026-10-03-routing-smoke.txt) and [baseline metadata](hermes/baseline.json). The raw local log remains `.local/hermes-lab/routing-smoke.log`.

Preflight also confirmed no upstream fallback `.env`, `/etc/hermes` managed directory, or personal `~/.hermes/pytest_live_guard.py` hook existed during this run. No upstream tracked file was changed.

## Next experiment

The workspace/app, owner-command connection and narrow owner model smoke are ready; [Slack setup](SLACK_SETUP.md) and [model smoke](MODEL_SMOKE.md) document their configuration. A first `gpt-5.4-mini` request failed with HTTP `400`; a live account catalog lookup identified `gpt-6-luna`, which passed CLI, owner DM and channel mention inference with zero tools. The failure remains in the evidence record.

The user-selected default is now `gpt-6.1-sol`; [CLI and owner Slack DM inference passed](evidence/2026-10-03-model-61-smoke.md) with zero tools. [The second controlled account accepted its invitation and signed in through Aside](evidence/2026-10-03-second-slack-user.md). It is an ordinary test-channel member; Hermes admission remains owner-only. [Colima/Lima installation is complete](RUNTIME_SETUP.md), but no VM was started: only 3.31 GiB was free and the data volume was 99% full. The immediate prerequisite is disk headroom, then verifying the runtime boundary and browser setup before [the first scenario](SCENARIO_V1.md). The foreground gateway used for the smoke is not a daemon or a hosted deployment. Reviewer funding remains unresolved.

Use configuration first, then supported extensions, and make the smallest code change only when recorded evidence requires it. Repeat failed and affected checks on the same pinned baseline before moving to hosted acceptance.

Sources: [pinned contributor setup](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/CONTRIBUTING.md), [dependency metadata](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/pyproject.toml), [canonical test runner](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f/scripts/run_tests.sh).
