# clanker v1 scope and build approach ## State **clanker v1 is a hosted Hermes-based Slack assistant for general browser tasks and access management. Reuse Hermes first; focus clanker-specific work on routing and authorization, and add code only for demonstrated gaps.** The repository contains this scope, a verification strategy and source review, plus a pinned stock Hermes local baseline and clanker Slack setup files. The local CLI starts, 47 targeted upstream routing/session tests pass, and real Slack owner commands work in a DM and the test channel; see [LOCAL_BASELINE.md](verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md). The full Slack/browser E2E, deployed reviewer experience, and v1 acceptance remain open. Upstream documentation and synthetic tests establish narrower capabilities, not that our chosen deployment has passed its requirements. **Selected browser architecture:** each assigned worker VM runs Hermes and local Chromium, controlled through Hermes's existing Browser Use driver. This is the selected v1 design; the VM pool, browser workflow, and persistence across VM replacement still require implementation and verification. **Selected access interface:** a hosted clanker vault web app uses Sign in with Slack to collect and manage saved access. Reuse Hermes's vault implementation and UI/API components behind clanker's authenticated owner and task checks. This integration is selected, not implemented or verified. The assignment permits third-party components and prioritizes a smooth working experience over code volume. A successful v1 may consist mostly of configuration, deployment, integration fixes, and verification. There is no requirement to build a new agent harness, Slack connector, browser engine, vault, or TOTP algorithm. Slack is the v1 conversation interface, with the hosted vault web app for secure access collection and management. The user reported that Sahan approved Slack identity replacing the assignment's Google-only chatbot sign-in requirement. Sahan and Nishank enter through the demo workspace invitation/entry link and use clanker without local setup or their own model-provider accounts. Inference is owner-funded. The assignment's core is browser tasks and secure access management. Private DMs, shared channel context, and protection between reviewers are additional v1 behavior requested by the user. A general self-service SaaS platform is not a prerequisite. ### Preferred inference setup: owner's ChatGPT account Prefer using the owner's existing ChatGPT subscription through Hermes's ChatGPT/Codex OAuth provider for the cloud baseline, to avoid purchasing separate API credits for eligible model usage. Reviewers still use Slack without their own model-provider accounts. This is the preferred setup to evaluate, not a verified funding arrangement. [Hermes documents](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers) device-code authorization, which lets the owner approve login in their browser while Hermes runs and stores its authentication on the cloud host. [OpenAI documents](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542-using-your-chatgpt-plan-in-other-apps-and-sites) eligible plan usage in supported integrations; Hermes's exact account eligibility and quota accounting remain unverified for this deployment. Before relying on this route, establish that the intended owner-funded reviewer usage is supported, run a small inference request, and inspect the resulting usage and billing. Verify authentication refresh and persistence across a cloud restart with the owner's laptop out of the execution path. Subscription-funded inference does not establish coverage for hosting or separately billed browser/tool services. Record those costs separately. Any alternative paid inference setup remains a separate decision if the preferred route cannot meet the requirements. ## Reuse from Hermes Pin the Hermes version and required integrations, configure them, and verify their behavior in the deployed Slack experience. | Capability | Starting point | What clanker must establish | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent harness | Hermes's agent loop, tools, skills, and session machinery | General tasks work with the selected model and enabled tools. | | Slack interface | Hermes's existing Slack adapter and gateway | App configuration, authenticated admission, correct conversation routing, and replies. | | Browser automation | Local Chromium inside the assigned worker VM, controlled by Hermes's existing Browser Use driver (`browser_exec`) | Background browser work, uploads/downloads, secure login/handoff, scoped browser persistence, and saved-access reuse across worker replacement. | | Credentials and 2FA | Hermes's credential vault, Desktop vault form/API components, protected browser filling, TOTP support, and access-management controls | The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack and enforces owner/task/site access before saving or using credentials. Reviewers can securely provide, reuse, and remove access. Resolve the TOTP choice below. | | Profiles and conversations | Existing profile routing, DM/channel/thread sessions, memory, and persistence | The selected configuration enforces the intended tenant, owner, and audience boundaries across turns and restarts. | Start from the documented [browser integration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/), [credential vault](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault/), [profile routing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways/#routing-shared-bot-chats-to-profiles-profile_routes), and [session behavior](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#shared-vs-isolated-group-sessions). Native vault UI/API components cover CLI/Desktop use; the selected hosted web app adds the Slack identity and access-request authorization boundary. The complete collection, reuse, and revocation flow still needs validation. ## Architecture and routing contract **Use a shared Slack gateway and a pool of isolated Hermes worker VMs.** The gateway binds authenticated tenant, sender, and conversation audience to an authorized profile before queueing the task. The scheduler assigns a ready VM to that private or shared context; the VM pool manager maintains clean warm spares, adds capacity within limits, and removes excess idle capacity. Each worker runs Hermes, its Browser Use driver, and local Chromium inside the same VM. Profiles and permitted browser/file state persist beyond the worker's lifetime. The hosting provider, pool sizes, idle timeout, and storage implementation remain open choices. ```mermaid flowchart TD Slack["Slack workspaces
Private DMs and shared channels/threads"] <--> Gateway["Hermes Slack gateway"] Gateway --> Routing["Authenticated tenant, sender, and audience
Bind authorized profile and task"] Routing --> Queue["Durable task queue + scheduler
Fair dispatch, leases, bounded retries"] Queue -->|Assign task| Worker["Assigned worker VM
Hermes + Browser Use driver + local Chromium
One authorized private or shared context"] Queue -->|Pending demand| Pool["VM pool manager / autoscaler
Ready-spare target, VM limits, idle timeout"] Pool -->|Lifecycle calls| Provider["VM provider API"] Provider -->|Provision or stop| Worker Worker -->|Capacity and health| Pool Worker <--> Access["Enforced resource access
Only the current context's authorized state"] Access <--> State["Durable profile home, browser state, and files
Separate task and delivery records"] Gateway -->|Private access link| VaultUI["Hosted clanker vault web app"] VaultUI <--> Auth["Sign in with Slack
OIDC identity + server session"] Auth -->|Verified workspace and user| Trusted["Trusted credential handler
Owner, task, site, and action checks"] VaultUI -->|Secure credential submission| Trusted Trusted <--> Vault["Protected durable Hermes vault
Keys inaccessible to agent code"] Access -->|Authorized credential operation| Trusted Trusted -->|Resume after durable save| Queue Worker -->|Persist result| Delivery["Result delivery + owner-bound approval enforcement"] Delivery --> Gateway ``` These boxes describe responsibilities, not mandatory separate services. Reuse Hermes's Slack adapter, agent runtime, browser driver, vault, and session machinery. Routing checks may use existing configuration, supported extension points, or a small clanker integration. The scheduler and VM pool manager can share a backend service. The remote worker-to-gateway handoff must bind and durably record results before releasing a worker; reuse existing Slack delivery where it fits. Run Hermes in its upstream runtime; TypeScript remains the preference for clanker-owned integration code where appropriate. ### Selected browser stack: local Chromium + Browser Use Use the existing [Browser Use driver](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/#browser-use-mode-default) with local Chromium. Hermes remains the agent making decisions; Browser Use supplies browser control through `browser_exec`. A hosted browser service is not part of the selected v1 baseline. Make local selection explicit instead of relying on credential autodetection: ```yaml browser: cloud_provider: local backend: browser-use ``` Build the worker image with pinned, compatible versions of Hermes, the Browser Use CLI, `agent-browser`, Chromium, and the required Linux dependencies. The pinned Hermes release installs/discovers the Browser Use CLI separately; pinning Hermes alone does not pin that driver. Complete installation during image construction so assigned tasks do not depend on first-use downloads. Keep **Hermes itself, the Python executed by `browser_exec`, and Chromium inside the assigned VM**. Running only the browser there would leave driver code executing on the shared host. Expose only the current context's authorized profile, browser state, and files; a shared channel worker must not receive a participant's private account state. Persist the authorized profile state, including `state.db` conversation and tool history, plus the dedicated browser profile and required workspace files/artifacts. Keep the protected vault and its decryption keys outside agent-accessible profile mounts, as specified below. Clanker's task record references the Hermes profile and session rather than duplicating chat history. Default local Chromium sessions are temporary, so configure and verify a persistent browser profile; a dedicated local Chromium instance connected through CDP is an existing integration option. The exact persistence mechanism remains to be validated. Restoring conversation history and cookies does not by itself restore a live page, unfinished form, or in-flight action. Before accepting this stack, exercise secure credential filling and human login/handoff, saved-login reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, download/inspection or transformation/upload, owner/audience separation, revocation, and recovery after worker replacement. These are pending acceptance checks, not capabilities already verified in clanker's local baseline. ### Selected access flow: hosted vault + Sign in with Slack Send the owner a private link to an expiring access request. The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack OpenID Connect and can reuse a valid server session for later visits. Validate the token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce, and validate OAuth state on the redirect. Match the verified Slack `team_id` and `user_id` to the request's tenant and owner; the server also binds the task, site origin, and permitted action. Reject a mismatched identity, expired request, or replay, and consume the request once on successful submission. Neither an email address, URL parameter, nor possession of the link grants access. This Sign in with Slack flow is separate from the Slack bot installation OAuth flow. Reuse Hermes's vault storage, validation, browser-fill/TOTP primitives, and existing Desktop form/API components where suitable. Clanker supplies the hosted page, authenticated session, request authorization, and task-resumption integration; exposing the general Hermes dashboard or accepting a client-selected profile is not that boundary. The existing optional setup-key field is reusable capability, not a decision to enable automatic TOTP; the product choice below remains unresolved. Submit secrets directly from the secure form to a trusted credential handler. Passwords and setup keys must bypass Slack, model inputs, task queue payloads, and application logs. The handler selects authorized storage from trusted identity, persists it durably, and returns only a handle and safe metadata. Keep the handler and decryption keys in an execution boundary inaccessible to arbitrary agent code; a context-local profile switch or a vault key beside agent-readable files does not enforce this. Authorized browser filling uses the protected path without returning the secret to the model. The exact boundary and Hermes integration require implementation and verification. Persist `waiting_for_input` and the access request independently of the worker VM. After a successful durable save, atomically consume the request and record the task's readiness for resumption, with idempotent dispatch so retries cannot lose or duplicate the resume transition. Requeue the original task with the credential handle, not the secret; an active worker need not remain online while the owner fills the form. Verify that saving during worker replacement resumes the correct task and that removing access prevents further affected credential use and saved-session reuse. | Routing decision | Required behavior | | --- | --- | | Tenant | Derive workspace/installation identity from authenticated Slack events. Include it in user, conversation, and resource routing. Reject unknown or unauthorized requesters instead of falling into a privileged default. | | Conversation and audience | A 1:1 DM loads that user's private context. A channel/thread loads context authorized for that channel's audience. Workspace membership alone does not reveal private-channel history. | | Requester and resource owner | Keep the sender, account/resource owner, and conversation audience distinct. Validate ownership before using credentials, browsers, files, history, or controls. Another participant's follow-up conveys no authority over someone else's private work. | | Context and tools | Scope memory, session recall, learned skills, files, artifacts, browser state, and credentials to the current authorized context. Prompt instructions and model-supplied owner IDs cannot grant access. | | Result destination | Return private account results privately. Sharing requires the owner's approval of the specific content and audience. Shared output grants no access to its source account or private files. | Session separation and profile routing are useful controls, but must be tested together with tools and persistence. Shared-profile memory or session recall must not expose DM content in a channel. Model-generated code must not have unrestricted access to other owners' files, the shared history store, or platform administrator credentials. Use supported scoped tools and isolated execution where needed; disable or adapt a tool whose access cannot be constrained. Keep retained history, recovery state, browser access, and artifacts durable across restarts, with their owner/audience associations intact. Use existing persistence when it meets these needs. The VM execution boundary and local browser stack above are selected; the cloud vendor, storage technology, and exact profile/session mapping remain implementation choices. For v1 delivery, the reviewers use one demo workspace. Routing must still carry tenant identity and be checked against another tenant identity without requiring a public onboarding or provisioning product. ### Example: collaboration involving a private account Sahan and Nishank discuss a report in a shared thread. Both contributions belong to that thread's context. If the work needs Sahan's private account, route that part into an owner-authorized private conversation/run, using existing capabilities where possible. Obtain missing authorization through his DM or secure handoff. Private observations never enter the shared conversation automatically. Sahan receives the result privately and may approve selected content for publication back into the thread. Nishank can continue the shared discussion without gaining authority over Sahan's account. ## Required behavior 1. **Perform general browser and file tasks.** Accept natural-language goals across different, unfamiliar websites. Discover and upload an intended existing file; support download, inspection/transformation, and upload when requested. Site-specific scripts are not evidence of general capability. 2. **Collect, reuse, and revoke access.** Support secure input or login handoff for passwords, API keys, OAuth/browser access, and card details when needed. Keep secrets out of chat and model inputs. Reuse encrypted saved access and browser sessions across tasks and fresh browser runs. Owners can remove access; affected active work and saved sessions must not silently retain the revoked authority. 3. **Preserve private and shared boundaries.** DMs, personal memory, credentials, browser state, and private files stay owner-scoped. Channel discussions and intentionally shared material stay audience-scoped. Concurrent users cannot take over each other's sessions, account access, private history, approvals, or artifacts. 4. **Work in the background and recover.** Acknowledge requests promptly, provide useful brief progress, clarify material details, and offer private human handoff when needed. Persist the task through expired access, failures, and restarts; resume without blindly replaying completed consequential actions. Support cancellation and bounded execution. 5. **Confirm and verify.** Obtain owner confirmation for concrete consequential actions such as purchases, external messages, publication, or deletion. Changed action details require fresh confirmation. Confirm the actual website state or artifact before reporting completion. Approval for an action and approval to share its private result are separate permissions. ### TOTP: existing capability, unresolved product choice Reuse Hermes's existing TOTP implementation if automatic generation is included. The user's preferred flow is to supply the current code through secure input or a private browser handoff, keeping the setup key with the user. Check shared collaboration and private boundaries using the actual enabled tools. Validate owner-bound resource selection and controlled result delivery instead of rebuilding passing upstream features. 5. **Validate the hosted experience and package the result.** Repeat the acceptance checks with the developer's laptop out of the execution path. Produce the repository, entry link, demo, and access-management note. Attribute Hermes and other reused components accurately. **Done when:** the required behavior works through the deployed reviewer experience, the four deliverables exist, and the release evidence passes. Code volume and the number of custom components are not completion criteria. Record unsupported or unresolved requirements explicitly; do not mark v1 complete while they remain unmet. ## Release evidence | Area | Evidence required | | --- | --- | | Inference authentication and funding | Verify the chosen ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route supports the owner's account and intended hosted reviewer use. # clanker v1 scope and build approach ## State **clanker v1 is a hosted Hermes-based Slack assistant for general browser tasks and access management. Reuse Hermes first; focus clanker-specific work on routing and authorization, and add code only for demonstrated gaps.** The repository contains this scope, a verification strategy and source review, plus a pinned stock Hermes local baseline and clanker Slack setup files. The local CLI starts, 47 targeted upstream routing/session tests pass, and real Slack owner commands work in a DM and the test channel; see [LOCAL_BASELINE.md](verification/LOCAL_BASELINE.md). The full Slack/browser E2E, deployed reviewer experience, and v1 acceptance remain open. Upstream documentation and synthetic tests establish narrower capabilities, not that our chosen deployment has passed its requirements. **Selected browser architecture:** each assigned worker VM runs Hermes and local Chromium, controlled through Hermes's existing Browser Use driver. This is the selected v1 design; the VM pool, browser workflow, and persistence across VM replacement still require implementation and verification. **Selected access interface:** a hosted clanker vault web app uses Sign in with Slack to collect and manage saved access. Reuse Hermes's vault implementation and UI/API components behind clanker's authenticated owner and task checks. This integration is selected, not implemented or verified. The assignment permits third-party components and prioritizes a smooth working experience over code volume. A successful v1 may consist mostly of configuration, deployment, integration fixes, and verification. There is no requirement to build a new agent harness, Slack connector, browser engine, vault, or TOTP algorithm. Slack is the v1 conversation interface, with the hosted vault web app for secure access collection and management. The user reported that Sahan approved Slack identity replacing the assignment's Google-only chatbot sign-in requirement. Sahan and Nishank enter through the demo workspace invitation/entry link and use clanker without local setup or their own model-provider accounts. Inference is owner-funded. The assignment's core is browser tasks and secure access management. Private DMs, shared channel context, and protection between reviewers are additional v1 behavior requested by the user. A general self-service SaaS platform is not a prerequisite. ### Preferred inference setup: owner's ChatGPT account Prefer using the owner's existing ChatGPT subscription through Hermes's ChatGPT/Codex OAuth provider for the cloud baseline, to avoid purchasing separate API credits for eligible model usage. Reviewers still use Slack without their own model-provider accounts. This is the preferred setup to evaluate, not a verified funding arrangement. [Hermes documents](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers) device-code authorization, which lets the owner approve login in their browser while Hermes runs and stores its authentication on the cloud host. [OpenAI documents](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001542-using-your-chatgpt-plan-in-other-apps-and-sites) eligible plan usage in supported integrations; Hermes's exact account eligibility and quota accounting remain unverified for this deployment. Before relying on this route, establish that the intended owner-funded reviewer usage is supported, run a small inference request, and inspect the resulting usage and billing. Verify authentication refresh and persistence across a cloud restart with the owner's laptop out of the execution path. Subscription-funded inference does not establish coverage for hosting or separately billed browser/tool services. Record those costs separately. Any alternative paid inference setup remains a separate decision if the preferred route cannot meet the requirements. ## Reuse from Hermes Pin the Hermes version and required integrations, configure them, and verify their behavior in the deployed Slack experience. | Capability | Starting point | What clanker must establish | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent harness | Hermes's agent loop, tools, skills, and session machinery | General tasks work with the selected model and enabled tools. | | Slack interface | Hermes's existing Slack adapter and gateway | App configuration, authenticated admission, correct conversation routing, and replies. | | Browser automation | Local Chromium inside the assigned worker VM, controlled by Hermes's existing Browser Use driver (`browser_exec`) | Background browser work, uploads/downloads, secure login/handoff, scoped browser persistence, and saved-access reuse across worker replacement. | | Credentials and 2FA | Hermes's credential vault, Desktop vault form/API components, protected browser filling, TOTP support, and access-management controls | The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack and enforces owner/task/site access before saving or using credentials. Reviewers can securely provide, reuse, and remove access. Resolve the TOTP choice below. | | Profiles and conversations | Existing profile routing, DM/channel/thread sessions, memory, and persistence | The selected configuration enforces the intended tenant, owner, and audience boundaries across turns and restarts. | Start from the documented [browser integration](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/), [credential vault](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault/), [profile routing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways/#routing-shared-bot-chats-to-profiles-profile_routes), and [session behavior](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/sessions/#shared-vs-isolated-group-sessions). Native vault UI/API components cover CLI/Desktop use; the selected hosted web app adds the Slack identity and access-request authorization boundary. The complete collection, reuse, and revocation flow still needs validation. ## Architecture and routing contract **Use a shared Slack gateway and a pool of isolated Hermes worker VMs.** The gateway binds authenticated tenant, sender, and conversation audience to an authorized profile before queueing the task. The scheduler assigns a ready VM to that private or shared context; the VM pool manager maintains clean warm spares, adds capacity within limits, and removes excess idle capacity. Each worker runs Hermes, its Browser Use driver, and local Chromium inside the same VM. Profiles and permitted browser/file state persist beyond the worker's lifetime. The hosting provider, pool sizes, idle timeout, and storage implementation remain open choices. ```mermaid flowchart TD Slack["Slack workspaces
Private DMs and shared channels/threads"] <--> Gateway["Hermes Slack gateway"] Gateway --> Routing["Authenticated tenant, sender, and audience
Bind authorized profile and task"] Routing --> Queue["Durable task queue + scheduler
Fair dispatch, leases, bounded retries"] Queue -->|Assign task| Worker["Assigned worker VM
Hermes + Browser Use driver + local Chromium
One authorized private or shared context"] Queue -->|Pending demand| Pool["VM pool manager / autoscaler
Ready-spare target, VM limits, idle timeout"] Pool -->|Lifecycle calls| Provider["VM provider API"] Provider -->|Provision or stop| Worker Worker -->|Capacity and health| Pool Worker <--> Access["Enforced resource access
Only the current context's authorized state"] Access <--> State["Durable profile home, browser state, and files
Separate task and delivery records"] Gateway -->|Private access link| VaultUI["Hosted clanker vault web app"] VaultUI <--> Auth["Sign in with Slack
OIDC identity + server session"] Auth -->|Verified workspace and user| Trusted["Trusted credential handler
Owner, task, site, and action checks"] VaultUI -->|Secure credential submission| Trusted Trusted <--> Vault["Protected durable Hermes vault
Keys inaccessible to agent code"] Access -->|Authorized credential operation| Trusted Trusted -->|Resume after durable save| Queue Worker -->|Persist result| Delivery["Result delivery + owner-bound approval enforcement"] Delivery --> Gateway ``` These boxes describe responsibilities, not mandatory separate services. Reuse Hermes's Slack adapter, agent runtime, browser driver, vault, and session machinery. Routing checks may use existing configuration, supported extension points, or a small clanker integration. The scheduler and VM pool manager can share a backend service. The remote worker-to-gateway handoff must bind and durably record results before releasing a worker; reuse existing Slack delivery where it fits. Run Hermes in its upstream runtime; TypeScript remains the preference for clanker-owned integration code where appropriate. ### Selected browser stack: local Chromium + Browser Use Use the existing [Browser Use driver](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/browser/#browser-use-mode-default) with local Chromium. Hermes remains the agent making decisions; Browser Use supplies browser control through `browser_exec`. A hosted browser service is not part of the selected v1 baseline. Make local selection explicit instead of relying on credential autodetection: ```yaml browser: cloud_provider: local backend: browser-use ``` Build the worker image with pinned, compatible versions of Hermes, the Browser Use CLI, `agent-browser`, Chromium, and the required Linux dependencies. The pinned Hermes release installs/discovers the Browser Use CLI separately; pinning Hermes alone does not pin that driver. Complete installation during image construction so assigned tasks do not depend on first-use downloads. Keep **Hermes itself, the Python executed by `browser_exec`, and Chromium inside the assigned VM**. Running only the browser there would leave driver code executing on the shared host. Expose only the current context's authorized profile, browser state, and files; a shared channel worker must not receive a participant's private account state. Persist the authorized profile state, including `state.db` conversation and tool history, plus the dedicated browser profile and required workspace files/artifacts. Keep the protected vault and its decryption keys outside agent-accessible profile mounts, as specified below. Clanker's task record references the Hermes profile and session rather than duplicating chat history. Default local Chromium sessions are temporary, so configure and verify a persistent browser profile; a dedicated local Chromium instance connected through CDP is an existing integration option. The exact persistence mechanism remains to be validated. Restoring conversation history and cookies does not by itself restore a live page, unfinished form, or in-flight action. Before accepting this stack, exercise secure credential filling and human login/handoff, saved-login reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, download/inspection or transformation/upload, owner/audience separation, revocation, and recovery after worker replacement. These are pending acceptance checks, not capabilities already verified in clanker's local baseline. ### Selected access flow: hosted vault + Sign in with Slack Send the owner a private link to an expiring access request. The hosted clanker vault web app authenticates with Slack OpenID Connect and can reuse a valid server session for later visits. Validate the token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce, and validate OAuth state on the redirect. Match the verified Slack `team_id` and `user_id` to the request's tenant and owner; the server also binds the task, site origin, and permitted action. Reject a mismatched identity, expired request, or replay, and consume the request once on successful submission. Neither an email address, URL parameter, nor possession of the link grants access. This Sign in with Slack flow is separate from the Slack bot installation OAuth flow. Reuse Hermes's vault storage, validation, browser-fill/TOTP primitives, and existing Desktop form/API components where suitable. Clanker supplies the hosted page, authenticated session, request authorization, and task-resumption integration; exposing the general Hermes dashboard or accepting a client-selected profile is not that boundary. The existing optional setup-key field is reusable capability, not a decision to enable automatic TOTP; the product choice below remains unresolved. Submit secrets directly from the secure form to a trusted credential handler. Passwords and setup keys must bypass Slack, model inputs, task queue payloads, and application logs. The handler selects authorized storage from trusted identity, persists it durably, and returns only a handle and safe metadata. Keep the handler and decryption keys in an execution boundary inaccessible to arbitrary agent code; a context-local profile switch or a vault key beside agent-readable files does not enforce this. Authorized browser filling uses the protected path without returning the secret to the model. The exact boundary and Hermes integration require implementation and verification. Persist `waiting_for_input` and the access request independently of the worker VM. After a successful durable save, atomically consume the request and record the task's readiness for resumption, with idempotent dispatch so retries cannot lose or duplicate the resume transition. Requeue the original task with the credential handle, not the secret; an active worker need not remain online while the owner fills the form. Verify that saving during worker replacement resumes the correct task and that removing access prevents further affected credential use and saved-session reuse. | Routing decision | Required behavior | | --- | --- | | Tenant | Derive workspace/installation identity from authenticated Slack events. Include it in user, conversation, and resource routing. Reject unknown or unauthorized requesters instead of falling into a privileged default. | | Conversation and audience | A 1:1 DM loads that user's private context. A channel/thread loads context authorized for that channel's audience. Workspace membership alone does not reveal private-channel history. | | Requester and resource owner | Keep the sender, account/resource owner, and conversation audience distinct. Validate ownership before using credentials, browsers, files, history, or controls. Another participant's follow-up conveys no authority over someone else's private work. | | Context and tools | Scope memory, session recall, learned skills, files, artifacts, browser state, and credentials to the current authorized context. Prompt instructions and model-supplied owner IDs cannot grant access. | | Result destination | Return private account results privately. Sharing requires the owner's approval of the specific content and audience. Shared output grants no access to its source account or private files. | Session separation and profile routing are useful controls, but must be tested together with tools and persistence. Shared-profile memory or session recall must not expose DM content in a channel. Model-generated code must not have unrestricted access to other owners' files, the shared history store, or platform administrator credentials. Use supported scoped tools and isolated execution where needed; disable or adapt a tool whose access cannot be constrained. Keep retained history, recovery state, browser access, and artifacts durable across restarts, with their owner/audience associations intact. Use existing persistence when it meets these needs. The VM execution boundary and local browser stack above are selected; the cloud vendor, storage technology, and exact profile/session mapping remain implementation choices. For v1 delivery, the reviewers use one demo workspace. Routing must still carry tenant identity and be checked against another tenant identity without requiring a public onboarding or provisioning product. ### Example: collaboration involving a private account Sahan and Nishank discuss a report in a shared thread. Both contributions belong to that thread's context. If the work needs Sahan's private account, route that part into an owner-authorized private conversation/run, using existing capabilities where possible. Obtain missing authorization through his DM or secure handoff. Private observations never enter the shared conversation automatically. Sahan receives the result privately and may approve selected content for publication back into the thread. Nishank can continue the shared discussion without gaining authority over Sahan's account. ## Required behavior 1. **Perform general browser and file tasks.** Accept natural-language goals across different, unfamiliar websites. Discover and upload an intended existing file; support download, inspection/transformation, and upload when requested. Site-specific scripts are not evidence of general capability. 2. **Collect, reuse, and revoke access.** Support secure input or login handoff for passwords, API keys, OAuth/browser access, and card details when needed. Keep secrets out of chat and model inputs. Reuse encrypted saved access and browser sessions across tasks and fresh browser runs. Owners can remove access; affected active work and saved sessions must not silently retain the revoked authority. 3. **Preserve private and shared boundaries.** DMs, personal memory, credentials, browser state, and private files stay owner-scoped. Channel discussions and intentionally shared material stay audience-scoped. Concurrent users cannot take over each other's sessions, account access, private history, approvals, or artifacts. 4. **Work in the background and recover.** Acknowledge requests promptly, provide useful brief progress, clarify material details, and offer private human handoff when needed. Persist the task through expired access, failures, and restarts; resume without blindly replaying completed consequential actions. Support cancellation and bounded execution. 5. **Confirm and verify.** Obtain owner confirmation for concrete consequential actions such as purchases, external messages, publication, or deletion. Changed action details require fresh confirmation. Confirm the actual website state or artifact before reporting completion. Approval for an action and approval to share its private result are separate permissions. ### TOTP: existing capability, unresolved product choice Reuse Hermes's existing TOTP implementation if automatic generation is included. The user's preferred flow is to supply the current code through secure input or a private browser handoff, keeping the setup key with the user. The original assignment explicitly requires accepting a TOTP setup key once and generating subsequent codes. **Manual code entry alone does not satisfy that criterion.** Resolve whether to demonstrate native automatic TOTP with the user's agreement or obtain an accepted assignment exception before declaring v1 complete. Automatic generation as an opt-in was discussed as a possibility, not settled. This choice does not require implementing a new TOTP algorithm and does not block the initial Slack/browser/routing proof. ## Now: build in this order 1. **Configure the selected local browser worker.** Pin Hermes and its browser dependencies, prepare a worker VM image with local Chromium and the Browser Use driver, enable the existing browser/vault capabilities, and provide reproducible setup and secret-free environment examples. Verify the chosen profile, browser, and workspace persistence arrangement. 2. **Configure routing and the secure access handoff.** Map verified workspace and sender identities to private DM or shared channel context and the correct resources. Build the selected vault web app and Slack sign-in flow around existing Hermes components, with owner-bound access requests and durable task resumption. Verify a two-user example, including denial of another user's access link. 3. **Exercise the complete reviewer flow.** From Slack, request browser work, provide access securely, reuse it, complete the file workflow, handle a failure, and remove access. Check shared collaboration and private boundaries using the actual enabled tools. Record passes, failures, and untested behavior. 4. **Fix remaining demonstrated gaps.** Prefer configuration, then supported plugins/extensions, then small integration changes beyond the selected hosted access flow. Validate owner-bound resource selection and controlled result delivery instead of rebuilding passing upstream features. 5. **Validate the hosted experience and package the result.** Repeat the acceptance checks with the developer's laptop out of the execution path. Produce the repository, entry link, demo, and access-management note. Attribute Hermes and other reused components accurately. **Done when:** the required behavior works through the deployed reviewer experience, the four deliverables exist, and the release evidence passes. Code volume and the number of custom components are not completion criteria. Record unsupported or unresolved requirements explicitly; do not mark v1 complete while they remain unmet. ## Release evidence | Area | Evidence required | | --- | --- | | Inference authentication and funding | Verify the chosen ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route supports the owner's account and intended hosted reviewer use. Record observed model-usage accounting and any separate charges. Exercise authentication refresh and restart persistence without depending on the owner's laptop. If this route is unavailable, record the unmet setup choice and agree an alternative before relying on it. | | General browser and file work | Complete real tasks on at least two different websites using the selected local Chromium + Browser Use stack inside the worker VM. Record driver/browser versions and confirm execution uses the local browser. Verify destination state independently of the agent's completion message. Find and upload the intended existing file, and complete download/inspection or transformation/upload. Treat two websites as an initial proof, not universal coverage. | | Access lifecycle | A reviewer signs into the hosted vault with Slack, securely connects access, and removes it. Reject wrong-user/wrong-workspace, expired, replayed, or altered access requests. Show secrets bypass chat/model/queue/logs and arbitrary agent code cannot read the vault's decryption keys. Verify durable save and resumption across worker replacement, saved-credential reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, and revocation of further affected access. Resolve and verify the TOTP criterion above. | | Recovery and durability | Exercise expired access or a controlled failure, supply the required input, and resume the original task. Restart the runtime and retain the correct history and artifacts. Verify recovery does not duplicate a completed consequential action. | | Routing, privacy, and collaboration | Two reviewers contribute to a shared task and retain its authorized context after restart. Test simultaneous private work, forged owner/tenant references, cross-user files/history/memory/skills, another participant's follow-up, and copied controls. Check that routing, enabled tools, and persisted data uphold the boundary, including another tenant identity. Demonstrate an approved result shared to a channel while private source data remains protected. | | Approvals and honest completion | Another participant cannot approve the owner's private action; changed action details or sharing audiences cannot reuse an old approval. Record actual outcomes, human intervention, failures, relevant versions, and known limits. Distinguish configured, verified, unsupported, and untested capabilities. | ## Four deliverables | Deliverable | Completion criteria | | --- | --- | | Runnable repository | Pinned dependencies/upstream versions, configuration, setup instructions, secret-free environment examples, and exercised verification instructions. Include integration code only where needed. | | Deployed reviewer experience | Slack invitation/entry link and hosted execution available without the developer's laptop. Two reviewers can use it without local setup or their own model-provider account. | | Approximately two-minute yyoreel demo | A real request, secure access collection or handoff, and verified completion. Include reuse/recovery where practical; inspect the exported video for exposed secrets before sharing. | | Access-management and known-limits note | Explain the chosen routing/profile/session boundaries, storage, access collection/reuse/revocation, TOTP decision, recovery, and verified limits. Identify upstream functionality versus clanker changes and explicitly disclose deferred operator/provider privacy controls. | ## Later Self-service multi-tenant onboarding/provisioning, additional messaging interfaces, delegated account access, advanced cross-team memory/grants, and configurable approval-policy UX are outside v1. Basic shared channel context, private DMs, ordinary owner confirmations, and approved result sharing remain in v1. Operator-access and model-provider-access privacy controls, including broader auditing, retention, training-use, and data-lifecycle controls, are deferred to clanker v2 or later as requested. This does not defer credential secrecy, protection between users/tenants, or honest disclosure of the deployed system's limits. ## Next Configure the selected local Chromium + Browser Use worker with Hermes's existing access capabilities, then prove the two-user DM/channel routing behavior and first complete browser task through Slack. Verify persistence across worker replacement and use those results to determine the remaining integration work. Settle the remaining TOTP choice before final acceptance. Obtain the user's review before external submission or contacting the founders.

Reuse Hermes's vault storage, validation, browser-fill/TOTP primitives, and existing Desktop form/API components where suitable. Clanker supplies the hosted page, authenticated session, request authorization, and task-resumption integration; exposing the general Hermes dashboard or accepting a client-selected profile is not that boundary. The existing optional setup-key field is reusable capability, not a decision to enable automatic TOTP; the product choice below remains unresolved. Submit secrets directly from the secure form to a trusted credential handler. Passwords and setup keys must bypass Slack, model inputs, task queue payloads, and application logs. The handler selects authorized storage from trusted identity, persists it durably, and returns only a handle and safe metadata. Keep the handler and decryption keys in an execution boundary inaccessible to arbitrary agent code; a context-local profile switch or a vault key beside agent-readable files does not enforce this. Authorized browser filling uses the protected path without returning the secret to the model. The exact boundary and Hermes integration require implementation and verification. Persist `waiting_for_input` and the access request independently of the worker VM. After a successful durable save, atomically consume the request and record the task's readiness for resumption, with idempotent dispatch so retries cannot lose or duplicate the resume transition. Requeue the original task with the credential handle, not the secret; an active worker need not remain online while the owner fills the form. Verify that saving during worker replacement resumes the correct task and that removing access prevents further affected credential use and saved-session reuse. | Routing decision | Required behavior | | --- | --- | | Tenant | Derive workspace/installation identity from authenticated Slack events. Include it in user, conversation, and resource routing. Reject unknown or unauthorized requesters instead of falling into a privileged default. | | Conversation and audience | A 1:1 DM loads that user's private context. A channel/thread loads context authorized for that channel's audience. Workspace membership alone does not reveal private-channel history. | | Requester and resource owner | Keep the sender, account/resource owner, and conversation audience distinct. Validate ownership before using credentials, browsers, files, history, or controls. Another participant's follow-up conveys no authority over someone else's private work. | | Context and tools | Scope memory, session recall, learned skills, files, artifacts, browser state, and credentials to the current authorized context. Prompt instructions and model-supplied owner IDs cannot grant access. | | Result destination | Return private account results privately. Sharing requires the owner's approval of the specific content and audience. Shared output grants no access to its source account or private files. | Session separation and profile routing are useful controls, but must be tested together with tools and persistence. Shared-profile memory or session recall must not expose DM content in a channel. Model-generated code must not have unrestricted access to other owners' files, the shared history store, or platform administrator credentials. Use supported scoped tools and isolated execution where needed; disable or adapt a tool whose access cannot be constrained. Keep retained history, recovery state, browser access, and artifacts durable across restarts, with their owner/audience associations intact. Use existing persistence when it meets these needs. The VM execution boundary and local browser stack above are selected; the cloud vendor, storage technology, and exact profile/session mapping remain implementation choices. For v1 delivery, the reviewers use one demo workspace. Routing must still carry tenant identity and be checked against another tenant identity without requiring a public onboarding or provisioning product. ### Example: collaboration involving a private account Sahan and Nishank discuss a report in a shared thread. Both contributions belong to that thread's context. If the work needs Sahan's private account, route that part into an owner-authorized private conversation/run, using existing capabilities where possible. Obtain missing authorization through his DM or secure handoff. Private observations never enter the shared conversation automatically. Sahan receives the result privately and may approve selected content for publication back into the thread. Nishank can continue the shared discussion without gaining authority over Sahan's account. ## Required behavior 1. **Perform general browser and file tasks.** Accept natural-language goals across different, unfamiliar websites. Discover and upload an intended existing file; support download, inspection/transformation, and upload when requested. Site-specific scripts are not evidence of general capability. 2. **Collect, reuse, and revoke access.** Support secure input or login handoff for passwords, API keys, OAuth/browser access, and card details when needed. Keep secrets out of chat and model inputs. Reuse encrypted saved access and browser sessions across tasks and fresh browser runs. Owners can remove access; affected active work and saved sessions must not silently retain the revoked authority. 3. **Preserve private and shared boundaries.** DMs, personal memory, credentials, browser state, and private files stay owner-scoped. Channel discussions and intentionally shared material stay audience-scoped. Concurrent users cannot take over each other's sessions, account access, private history, approvals, or artifacts. 4. **Work in the background and recover.** Acknowledge requests promptly, provide useful brief progress, clarify material details, and offer private human handoff when needed. Persist the task through expired access, failures, and restarts; resume without blindly replaying completed consequential actions. Support cancellation and bounded execution. 5. **Confirm and verify.** Obtain owner confirmation for concrete consequential actions such as purchases, external messages, publication, or deletion. Changed action details require fresh confirmation. Confirm the actual website state or artifact before reporting completion. Approval for an action and approval to share its private result are separate permissions. ### TOTP: existing capability, unresolved product choice Reuse Hermes's existing TOTP implementation if automatic generation is included. The user's preferred flow is to supply the current code through secure input or a private browser handoff, keeping the setup key with the user. The original assignment explicitly requires accepting a TOTP setup key once and generating subsequent codes. **Manual code entry alone does not satisfy that criterion.** Resolve whether to demonstrate native automatic TOTP with the user's agreement or obtain an accepted assignment exception before declaring v1 complete. Automatic generation as an opt-in was discussed as a possibility, not settled. This choice does not require implementing a new TOTP algorithm and does not block the initial Slack/browser/routing proof. ## Now: build in this order 1. **Configure the selected local browser worker.** Pin Hermes and its browser dependencies, prepare a worker VM image with local Chromium and the Browser Use driver, enable the existing browser/vault capabilities, and provide reproducible setup and secret-free environment examples. Verify the chosen profile, browser, and workspace persistence arrangement. 2. **Configure routing and the secure access handoff.** Map verified workspace and sender identities to private DM or shared channel context and the correct resources. Build the selected vault web app and Slack sign-in flow around existing Hermes components, with owner-bound access requests and durable task resumption. Verify a two-user example, including denial of another user's access link. 3. **Exercise the complete reviewer flow.** From Slack, request browser work, provide access securely, reuse it, complete the file workflow, handle a failure, and remove access. Check shared collaboration and private boundaries using the actual enabled tools. Record passes, failures, and untested behavior. 4. **Fix remaining demonstrated gaps.** Prefer configuration, then supported plugins/extensions, then small integration changes beyond the selected hosted access flow. Validate owner-bound resource selection and controlled result delivery instead of rebuilding passing upstream features. 5. **Validate the hosted experience and package the result.** Repeat the acceptance checks with the developer's laptop out of the execution path. Produce the repository, entry link, demo, and access-management note. Attribute Hermes and other reused components accurately. **Done when:** the required behavior works through the deployed reviewer experience, the four deliverables exist, and the release evidence passes. Code volume and the number of custom components are not completion criteria. Record unsupported or unresolved requirements explicitly; do not mark v1 complete while they remain unmet. ## Release evidence | Area | Evidence required | | --- | --- | | Inference authentication and funding | Verify the chosen ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route supports the owner's account and intended hosted reviewer use. Record observed model-usage accounting and any separate charges. Exercise authentication refresh and restart persistence without depending on the owner's laptop. If this route is unavailable, record the unmet setup choice and agree an alternative before relying on it. | | General browser and file work | Complete real tasks on at least two different websites using the selected local Chromium + Browser Use stack inside the worker VM. Record driver/browser versions and confirm execution uses the local browser. Verify destination state independently of the agent's completion message. Find and upload the intended existing file, and complete download/inspection or transformation/upload. Treat two websites as an initial proof, not universal coverage. | | Access lifecycle | A reviewer signs into the hosted vault with Slack, securely connects access, and removes it. Reject wrong-user/wrong-workspace, expired, replayed, or altered access requests. Show secrets bypass chat/model/queue/logs and arbitrary agent code cannot read the vault's decryption keys. Verify durable save and resumption across worker replacement, saved-credential reuse in a fresh browser, saved-session reuse separately, and revocation of further affected access. Resolve and verify the TOTP criterion above. | | Recovery and durability | Exercise expired access or a controlled failure, supply the required input, and resume the original task. Restart the runtime and retain the correct history and artifacts. Verify recovery does not duplicate a completed consequential action. | | Routing, privacy, and collaboration | Two reviewers contribute to a shared task and retain its authorized context after restart. Test simultaneous private work, forged owner/tenant references, cross-user files/history/memory/skills, another participant's follow-up, and copied controls. Check that routing, enabled tools, and persisted data uphold the boundary, including another tenant identity. Demonstrate an approved result shared to a channel while private source data remains protected. | | Approvals and honest completion | Another participant cannot approve the owner's private action; changed action details or sharing audiences cannot reuse an old approval. Record actual outcomes, human intervention, failures, relevant versions, and known limits. Distinguish configured, verified, unsupported, and untested capabilities. | ## Four deliverables | Deliverable | Completion criteria | | --- | --- | | Runnable repository | Pinned dependencies/upstream versions, configuration, setup instructions, secret-free environment examples, and exercised verification instructions. Include integration code only where needed. | | Deployed reviewer experience | Slack invitation/entry link and hosted execution available without the developer's laptop. Two reviewers can use it without local setup or their own model-provider account. | | Approximately two-minute yyoreel demo | A real request, secure access collection or handoff, and verified completion. Include reuse/recovery where practical; inspect the exported video for exposed secrets before sharing. | | Access-management and known-limits note | Explain the chosen routing/profile/session boundaries, storage, access collection/reuse/revocation, TOTP decision, recovery, and verified limits. Identify upstream functionality versus clanker changes and explicitly disclose deferred operator/provider privacy controls. | ## Later Self-service multi-tenant onboarding/provisioning, additional messaging interfaces, delegated account access, advanced cross-team memory/grants, and configurable approval-policy UX are outside v1. Basic shared channel context, private DMs, ordinary owner confirmations, and approved result sharing remain in v1. Operator-access and model-provider-access privacy controls, including broader auditing, retention, training-use, and data-lifecycle controls, are deferred to clanker v2 or later as requested. This does not defer credential secrecy, protection between users/tenants, or honest disclosure of the deployed system's limits. ## Next Configure the selected local Chromium + Browser Use worker with Hermes's existing access capabilities, then prove the two-user DM/channel routing behavior and first complete browser task through Slack.
